row_snapshot.title: What Is a Trust?
row_snapshot.summary: Introductory overview of what a trust is, why it exists, and the major parties involved.
row_snapshot.body: A trust is a legal relationship in which one party holds or manages property for the benefit of another according to defined terms. Common roles include settlor, trustee, and beneficiary.

row_snapshot.title: Roles in Trust Administration
row_snapshot.summary: Explains settlor, trustee, beneficiary, fiduciary, and related administrative roles.
row_snapshot.body: Trust administration depends on clearly defined roles. The settlor creates the trust, the trustee administers it, and the beneficiary receives benefit according to the trust terms.

row_snapshot.title: Revocable vs Irrevocable Trusts
row_snapshot.summary: Side-by-side conceptual comparison of revocable and irrevocable trusts.
row_snapshot.body: Revocable trusts generally allow modification during life, while irrevocable trusts are generally structured for permanence and reduced unilateral change. Exact consequences depend on governing law and trust terms.

row_snapshot.title: Land Trust Overview
row_snapshot.summary: Introduces land trust structure in relation to title holding and property management planning.
row_snapshot.body: Land trusts are commonly discussed where real property holding structure is central. They should be studied together with trustee roles, title handling, and reporting implications.

row_snapshot.title: Insurance Trust Overview
row_snapshot.summary: Introduces insurance trust structure and policy ownership planning concepts.
row_snapshot.body: Insurance trusts are often studied where policy ownership and insurance-related planning structure are central considerations.

row_snapshot.title: Simple vs Complex Trusts
row_snapshot.summary: Compares the concepts commonly associated with simple and complex trust classifications.
row_snapshot.body: Simple and complex trust discussions are often linked to distribution patterns, retained activity, and broader reporting implications.

row_snapshot.title: Fiduciary Duties in Practice
row_snapshot.summary: Practical overview of fiduciary administration duties inside a trust system.
row_snapshot.body: Fiduciary duties include recordkeeping, acting within granted authority, following the governing terms, and maintaining accountability across reports and decisions.

row_snapshot.title: Trust Administration Basics
row_snapshot.summary: A starter guide explaining the basic records and workflow surfaces used in the Trustee App.
row_snapshot.body: This article introduces trust identity, parties, property mapping, minutes, certificates, and packet review as separate workflow layers.
row_snapshot.related_forms: Trust Minutes, Certificate Registry, Formation Preview Hub

row_snapshot.title: Execution Certificates and Audit Trails
row_snapshot.summary: A starter guide for understanding executed minutes, certificate IDs, packet exports, and audit trail records.
row_snapshot.body: Execution certificates summarize completed governance records and connect them to signer roles, packet exports, and audit trail entries.

row_snapshot.summary: U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts.
row_snapshot.body: Form 1041 is generally used to report income, deductions, gains, losses, and distributions for trusts and estates. Whether it applies depends on structure and activity.
Form 1040 is the main individual income tax return. It may still matter in broader trust/estate planning discussions when individual and fiduciary matters intersect.

row_snapshot.summary: Amended return workflow for trust and estate returns.
row_snapshot.body: Use this guide page to track and explain amended return workflow for trust and estate filings where applicable.

row_snapshot.summary: Credit for Prior Year Minimum Tax.
row_snapshot.body: Form 8841 concerns prior year minimum tax credit issues. It should be treated as a supporting form guide and linked carefully to the relevant tax context.
Form 56 is used in fiduciary relationship contexts and should be understood together with trust administration and authority notice workflow.

row_snapshot.summary: Power of attorney and declaration of representative guide.
row_snapshot.body: Form 2848 is often studied when understanding authority delegation and representative appointment issues.

row_snapshot.applies_to: Entity address and responsible party changes
row_snapshot.summary: Change of address or responsible party update guide.
row_snapshot.body: Form 8822-B is relevant when entity identification or address details change and must be maintained accurately.
Schedule K-1 is commonly associated with reporting beneficiary allocations and should be studied together with trust distribution workflow.

row_snapshot.applies_to: Trustee decisions, approvals, executions, and archived governance records.
row_snapshot.summary: Explains how trust minutes preserve decisions and connect to execution certificates.
row_snapshot.body: Use trust minutes to record trustee decisions, approval, execution, signer capacity, and certificate generation.

row_snapshot.applies_to: Executed or archived trust minutes with certificate IDs.
row_snapshot.summary: Explains how the certificate registry indexes executed trust records.
row_snapshot.body: The certificate registry lists certificate IDs, minute references, execution status, packet exports, and verification links.
